investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-03T17:05–17:12Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a schedulable state, so the expected-output contract was violated in full.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidenced in failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, and sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable node exists for any remote-agent pod. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"). Because the pod never scheduled, the runner in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885: createAgent with machineType "remote") never received an agent identity, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource pool on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero allocatable capacity for new pods. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist.

[Possible] The 4 remaining nodes have a node affinity or label selector mismatch (e.g., missing a required label such as a kata/peerpods node label) that permanently excludes them from scheduling remote-agent pods, concentrating all capacity pressure on only 2 nodes.

[Possible] A recent scale-down, node failure, or node drain reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a higher count to 2, shrinking available capacity without a corresponding reduction in demand.

[Less likely] A resource quota or limit range at the namespace level is preventing new pod admission even when node capacity exists, but the scheduler message specifically names node-level resource insufficiency rather than quota rejection.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-03T17:05–17:12Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a schedulable state, so the expected-output contract was violated in full.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidenced in failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, and sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable node exists for any remote-agent pod. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"). Because the pod never scheduled, the runner in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885: createAgent with machineType "remote") never received an agent identity, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-03 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes have only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which are fully exhausted, and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or exercising the runtime, so zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were returned and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing remote agent provisioning in production-api has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two eligible nodes. Every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for 136–145 seconds before the eval timed out. Because pod scheduling never succeeded, the createAgent call in the eval runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never completed, no agent was created, and the expected-output contract requiring orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message was entirely unmet. The root cause is VM-slot exhaustion on the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, not an application code defect.
